sections.heading: Request → Work → Result → Payment
sections.text: THE LOOP Request → Work → Result → Payment One flow, four states, zero improvisation. The Space decides what may happen; the chain records what did. 01 Request a person creates A founder or teammate files a bounded request inside the Space. Intent is explicit before any money is in play. 02 Work a provider takes it Creating the Work Order escrows budget out of the Space treasury. Funds are committed, not spendable. 03 Result proof is required The provider submits a verifiable deliverable hash. No proof, no payout — approval is gated on evidence. 04 Payment an evaluator approves Approval settle

sections.heading: People and software side by side.
sections.text: ONE SPACE, EVERYONE IN People and software side by side. One Space holds five kinds of participant. The ontology is the point: a founder, an autonomous agent, a service, a partner organization, and a vendor all appear in the same ledger with the same standing. 01 Human Founders, operators, and the people who own the outcome. 02 Agent Autonomous workers inside the same rules, with the same ceiling. 03 Service APIs, daemons, and scheduled jobs that do the work. 04 Organization Teams and companies working under one shared agreement. 05 Counterparty The vendors payments are allowed to reach.

sections.heading: One agreement, enforced equally .
sections.text: RULES EVERYONE CAN SEE One agreement, enforced equally . Caps, budgets, allowlists, and balances are written where everyone can read them, then checked deterministically before any signature exists. The rules do not care who is asking. POLICY MATRIX · EXCERPT Per-transaction cap $500.00 any requester Daily budget $2,000.00 cumulative, resets daily Approved counterparties 3 allowlisted before use Treasury balance $4,530.00 shared, spendable DENIED · SAME VERDICT FOR ANYONE A $900 purchase that never happened A request to buy a $900 workstation came through the Space. The cap is $500. The policy

sections.heading: Every work order, on the board.
sections.text: LIVE WORK Every work order, on the board. Funded means escrowed. Submitted means a deliverable hash exists. Completed means the evaluator approved and payment settled on X Layer — bound to that exact hash. The board is the money.
